headline_marked: Amad Diallo's 90th-minute goal: [[Ivory Coast edge Ecuador 1-0]] in World Cup opener
headline: Amad Diallo's 90th-minute goal: Ivory Coast edge Ecuador 1-0 in World Cup opener
summary: Manchester United's Amad Diallo secured a dramatic late victory for the African champions in Philadelphia, marking their first World Cup win in 12 years.
details: Manchester United's Amad Diallo scored in the 90th minute to give Ivory Coast a 1-0 victory over Ecuador in their World Cup opener on Sunday.
The match, held at a packed Philadelphia stadium with 68,274 spectators, seemed destined for a goalless draw until Diallo's first-time finish from a right-wing cross just before injury time.
This victory marks Ivory Coast's first World Cup win in 12 years, their last being against Japan in 2014, and puts them in a strong position to reach the knockout phase.
Ecuador dominated much of the early game and hit the woodwork twice in the first half through John Yeboah and Alan Minda, while Ivory Coast's Elye Wahi also struck the bar after the restart.
Ecuador entered the tournament with a formidable defensive record, having conceded only five goals in 18 qualifying matches, but they were unable to hold off the late Ivorian surge.
Ivory Coast, the 2024 African champions, will now face Germany in their next Group E match in Toronto this Saturday.
Ecuador will look to recover from the disappointing start when they play Curacao in Kansas City on the same day.
caption:
A 90th-minute stunner! Amad Diallo seals a dramatic 1-0 win for Ivory Coast over Ecuador.

Manchester United's Amad Diallo scored in the 90th minute to give Ivory Coast a 1-0 victory over Ecuador in their World Cup opener on Sunday.

The match, held at a packed Philadelphia stadium with 68,274 spectators, seemed destined for a goalless draw until Diallo's first-time finish from a right-wing cross just before injury time.

This victory marks Ivory Coast's first World Cup win in 12 years, their last being against Japan in 2014, and puts them in a strong position to reach the knockout phase.

Ecuador dominated much of the early game and hit the woodwork twice in the first half through John Yeboah and Alan Minda, while Ivory Coast's Elye Wahi also struck the bar after the restart.

Ecuador entered the tournament with a formidable defensive record, having conceded only five goals in 18 qualifying matches, but they were unable to hold off the late Ivorian surge.

Ivory Coast, the 2024 African champions, will now face Germany in their next Group E match in Toronto this Saturday.

Ecuador will look to recover from the disappointing start when they play Curacao in Kansas City on the same day.

headline_marked: 239 goals: [[Germany overtakes Brazil]] as World Cup's all-time top scorers
headline: 239 goals: Germany overtakes Brazil as World Cup's all-time top scorers
summary: A dominant 7-1 victory over Curacao in their 2026 opening match pushes the four-time champions to the top of the scoring charts.
details: Germany has climbed to the top of the all-time FIFA World Cup scoring charts after a crushing 7-1 win against Curacao in their opening match of the 2026 tournament.
The victory took Germany's total to 239 goals, leapfrogging Brazil, who previously held the record with 237 goals. Brazil now sits second with 238 goals, while Argentina follows in third with 152.

The match saw Felix Nmecha score the fastest goal of the 2026 World Cup so far, netting after just six minutes. Curacao briefly equalized in the 21st minute through Livano Comenencia, marking the island nation's first-ever World Cup goal.
Germany regained control quickly with goals from Nico Schlotterbeck, Kai Havertz (2), Jamal Musiala, Nathaniel Brown, and Deniz Undav to secure the 7-1 triumph.
The game was historic for Curacao as well, as they became the smallest country by population and land area to ever appear at a World Cup finals.
Additionally, veteran Dutchman Dick Advocaat, aged 78, set a new record as the oldest coach in the tournament's history while leading Curacao.
Germany has now scored 239 goals across 113 matches and 21 tournaments. Brazil can potentially reclaim the top spot when they face Haiti in their second Group E match.
Germany's next match in Group E is against Ivory Coast on Saturday, followed by a final group-stage game against Ecuador.
caption:
Germany just broke the all-time World Cup scoring record! ⚽️

A dominant 7-1 win over Curacao pushes them past Brazil.

Germany has climbed to the top of the all-time FIFA World Cup scoring charts after a crushing 7-1 win against Curacao in their opening match of the 2026 tournament.

The victory took Germany's total to 239 goals, leapfrogging Brazil, who previously held the record with 237 goals. Brazil now sits second with 238 goals, while Argentina follows in third with 152.

The match saw Felix Nmecha score the fastest goal of the 2026 World Cup so far, netting after just six minutes. Curacao briefly equalized in the 21st minute through Livano Comenencia, marking the island nation's first-ever World Cup goal.

Germany regained control quickly with goals from Nico Schlotterbeck, Kai Havertz (2), Jamal Musiala, Nathaniel Brown, and Deniz Undav to secure the 7-1 triumph.

The game was historic for Curacao as well, as they became the smallest country by population and land area to ever appear at a World Cup finals.

Additionally, veteran Dutchman Dick Advocaat, aged 78, set a new record as the oldest coach in the tournament's history while leading Curacao.

Germany has now scored 239 goals across 113 matches and 21 tournaments. Brazil can potentially reclaim the top spot when they face Haiti in their second Group E match.

Germany's next match in Group E is against Ivory Coast on Saturday, followed by a final group-stage game against Ecuador.
